stage1.note: pcA and pc differ ONLY in the stacker slot, so the four cell argmins and the OOF npz must repeat exactly; that is a determinism check on the whole cell + OOF path

identity_anchor.what: the control arm is the exp_042 winner on all five models, so running it through the new per-model code must reproduce exp_042's stored fold_2024 predictions byte for byte

sigma_and_verdict.recipe: sigma = std(ddof=1) of the CONTROL arm's nine fold_2024 valid_all Brier values, converted to score units. Registered in prereg.json before any value existed.
sigma_and_verdict.verdict_rule: ADOPT requires all nine per-seed deltas to share a sign AND |mean delta| >= 3 sigma AND that sign to favour the treatment. Anything else rejects.
sigma_and_verdict.forward_only: this sigma applies from exp_045 onward; no past verdict is recomputed with it
sigma_and_verdict.scope: valid for this base and this feature set only

phase2_stacker_wide_only_bug.what: prereg.json and config.yaml both require the phase-2 stacker search to draw ALL 55 screen trials from the WIDE space only ('space schedule' wide_frac=1.0, comment in hpo044.py: 'the stacker is wide only'). The actual run split 27 narrow / 28 wide (schedule_counts in searches.stacker), i.e. roughly half the trials silently drew from the NARROW (cell-region) space -- exactly the mistake this experiment was designed to fix.
phase2_stacker_wide_only_bug.root_cause: wide_indices(n_trials=55, frac=1.0) computes k=round(55*1.0)=55, then widx = sorted({round((j+0.5)*55/55) for j in range(55)}) = sorted({round(j+0.5) for j in range(55)}). Python 3 round() uses round-half-to-even on exact .5 values, so round(0.5)=0, round(1.5)=2, round(2.5)=2, round(3.5)=4, ... -- consecutive half-integers collapse onto the same even integer, so the SET has only 28 distinct members instead of the intended 55. Every schedule index NOT in that 28-member set silently fell back to 'narrow' in `schedule = ["wide" if i in widx else "narrow" ...]`. The cell searches (frac=0.25, k=14) do not hit this collapse (verified: schedule_counts narrow=41/wide=14 for all four cells, matching the prereg's stated 41/14 split exactly) -- this bug is specific to the frac=1.0 (stacker-only) code path.
phase2_stacker_wide_only_bug.confirmation: the stacker's confirmed winner (screen_index=25, screen_rank 3, confirm_rank 1) has space='narrow' and params learning_rate=0.008273, rsm=0.46571 -- BOTH strictly below the wide space's declared lower bounds (learning_rate>=0.01, rsm>=0.5). These values are impossible draws from suggest_wide(); they can only have come from suggest_narrow() (learning_rate 0.008-0.030, rsm 0.45-0.95). This is a direct, checkable proof that the promoted stacker setting came out of the unintended narrow space, not the wide space the prereg promised.
phase2_stacker_wide_only_bug.consequence_for_this_experiment: the top-line phase-3 verdict is REJECT regardless (|mean delta| = 0.85 sigma, far under the 3-sigma bar, and signs split 6/3) -- a corrected wide-only rerun of the stacker search would not plausibly flip that verdict given the margin. But the phase-2 deliverable 'stacker winner vs cell winners, wide-space-only as promised' is NOT what was actually measured: the promoted stacker hyperparameters are contaminated by exactly the cell-region inheritance the experiment set out to avoid. Cell searches (four of them) are unaffected -- verified schedule_counts match prereg for all four.
phase2_stacker_wide_only_bug.not_fixed_here: this was found during report assembly, after the promotion run had already consumed the (contaminated) stacker pick. No code was changed and no search was rerun without the coordinator's decision -- fixing wide_indices() and rerunning phase 2's stacker search alone (~1.5-2h) is a follow-up the coordinator should decide on, not something this run self-corrected.
